run.change_description: fix(utils/body,validator): normalize Content-Type media type for case-insensitive matching

summary.intent: Make Content-Type media-type matching case-insensitive in parseBody(), validator() and bufferToFormData() while keeping parameters such as the multipart boundary intact (issue #5060).
summary.issue_fit: Mostly met: mixed-case JSON, urlencoded and multipart now match and the boundary is preserved. Separately, the rewritten parseFormData regresses parseBody() after a prior c.req.formData().
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff (6 files) read; callers in src/request.ts and src/validator/validator.ts inspected. Focused vitest run once at the head over body, buffer, validator and request tests: 144 passed, 1 skipped. Scratch probe compared head with base extracted by git archive; the regression reproduces at head only.

findings.title: Reuse cached FormData in parseBody instead of re-reading the body
findings.trigger: A handler or middleware calls `await c.req.formData()` and then `await c.req.parseBody()` on the same request. `parseFormData` now calls `arrayBuffer()`; with no arrayBuffer cached, `HonoRequest#cachedBody` re-serializes the cached FormData into a new multipart body with a fresh boundary, which is parsed against the original Content-Type.
findings.impact: Multipart requests make `parseBody()` reject with `TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.`; urlencoded requests silently return garbage keys such as `------formdata-undici-...`. At base both returned `{ foo: 'bar' }`.
findings.change: In `parseFormData`, when the request is a `HonoRequest` with `bodyCache.formData` set, await that value (as `src/validator/validator.ts` does) before falling back to `arrayBuffer()` and `bufferToFormData`.

observations.fact: After `parseBody()` the first `bodyCache` key is now `arrayBuffer` rather than `formData`, so `c.req.text()`, `c.req.json()` and `cloneRawRequest` read the raw bytes afterwards, and the multipart bytes stay cached for the request lifetime.
